Issue Title: Issues with writing file names

Description:
Hi, great tool!

I just starting trying it, and I'm running into some issues. 

Initially, I was encountering the same problem as detailed in this issue: https://github.com/AntonOsika/gpt-engineer/issues/167. Fortunately, I noticed you fixed this and after pulling the changes, that issue was resolved.

However, I'm now facing another issue related to file name generation. The program is formatting file names as '`filename`':
![image](https://github.com/AntonOsika/gpt-engineer/assets/25695071/6fe9db63-3b14-481d-8182-8c8ed5e9f75f)

At other (most) times, it's formatting them as '[filename]', which is resulting in file outputs like this:

![image](https://github.com/AntonOsika/gpt-engineer/assets/25695071/801f1da0-6968-4001-9bba-882d0db40c42)

I suspect this might have something to do with this commit: https://github.com/AntonOsika/gpt-engineer/commit/8180f0346c8a380637b72212432aa9abd5c04a9c#diff-945067bb601867dd64fd5ae92de9bf829da8545700835ac49744902ddec355fd

I'm using gpt-3.5-turbo since I don't have access to gpt-4 yet. Maybe the model is not as smart to understand this prompt?

Here are the possible buggy locations collected by someone else. Each location contains the actual code snippet and the intended behavior of the code for resolving the issue. Location #1: gpt_engineer/chat_to_files.py None parse_chat 4 def parse_chat(chat): # -> List[Tuple[str, str]]: 5 # Get all ``` blocks and preceding filenames 6 regex = r"(\S+?)\n```\S+\n(.+?)```" 7 matches = re.finditer(regex, chat, re.DOTALL) 8 9 files = [] 10 for match in matches: 11 # Strip the filename of any non-allowed characters and convert / to \ 12 path = re.sub(r'[<>"|?*]', "", match.group(1)) 13 14 # Get the code 15 code = match.group(2) 16 17 # Add the file to the list 18 files.append((path, code)) 19 20 # Get all the text before the first ``` block 21 readme = chat.split("```")[0] 22 files.append(("README.md", readme)) 23 24 # Return the files 25 return files The parse_chat function should be updated to accurately extract filenames without including enclosing backticks (`) or square brackets ([]). This can be done by modifying the regex or by stripping these markdown formatting characters from the matched filename before sanitizing and using it. The function should continue to strip invalid filesystem characters and correctly parse the code blocks, preserving existing functionality while ensuring filenames are clean and consistently formatted to prevent output files named with extraneous enclosing characters. The problem is that the filenames extracted from the chat sometimes include markdown formatting characters such as backticks (`) or square brackets ([]), resulting in output files named literally with those characters included (e.g., "`filename`" or "[filename]"). The regex currently captures the filename as a sequence of non-whitespace characters right before a code block, but does not strip the enclosing formatting characters like ` or [].

To fix this, we should strip enclosing backticks and square brackets from the matched filename before sanitizing it. This ensures the filename is clean and consistent irrespective of minor formatting differences in the chat.

The minimal change is to add a line that strips one pair of enclosing backticks or square brackets around the matched filename, before doing the existing sanitization.

```
<file>gpt_engineer/chat_to_files.py</file>
<original>4 def parse_chat(chat):  # -> List[Tuple[str, str]]:
5     # Get all ``` blocks and preceding filenames

10     for match in matches:
11         # Strip the filename of any non-allowed characters and convert / to \

13

16

18         files.append((path, code))
19

22     files.append(("README.md", readme))
23

</original>
<patched>4 def parse_chat(chat):  # -> List[Tuple[str, str]]:
5     # Get all ``` blocks and preceding filenames
6     regex = r"(\S+?)\n```\S+\n(.+?)```"
7     matches = re.finditer(regex, chat, re.DOTALL)
8 
9     files = []
10     for match in matches:
11         # Get raw filename
12         raw_path = match.group(1).strip()
13         
14         # Remove enclosing backticks or square brackets if present
15         if (raw_path.startswith("`") and raw_path.endswith("`")) or (raw_path.startswith("[") and raw_path.endswith("]")):
16             raw_path = raw_path[1:-1]
17 
18         # Strip the filename of any non-allowed characters
19         path = re.sub(r'[<>"|?*]', "", raw_path)
20 
21         # Get the code
22         code = match.group(2)
23 
24         # Add the file to the list
25         files.append((path, code))
26 
27     # Get all the text before the first ``` block
28     readme = chat.split("```")[0]
29     files.append(("README.md", readme))
30

32     return files
